title: Compute random alloy baseline monomer and dimer fractions
action: Analytically compute the expected monomer fraction (1-θ)^4 and dimer fraction 4θ(1-θ)^6 for a non-interacting fcc(100) surface alloy at θ=0.15. Save the results in a JSON file random_baseline.json.
description: Intermediate artifact containing the analytically computed random alloy monomer and dimer fractions.

title: Run Monte Carlo simulations for AuPd and AuPt surface alloys
action: Implement canonical (NVT) Monte Carlo simulation on a 30×30 fcc(100) lattice with periodic boundary conditions. Use the cluster expansion Hamiltonians (effective cluster interactions up to third nearest neighbour) for AuPd/Pd(100) and AuPt/Pt(100) from the Supporting Information to evaluate configuration energies every trial swap. Run simulations for four condition sets: (i) AuPd at θ=0.15, T=300 K; (ii) AuPt at θ=0.15, T=300 K; (iii) AuPd at θ=0.10, T=300 K; (iv) AuPd at θ=0.50, T=100 K. After equilibration, collect ensemble-averaged statistics: monomer and dimer counts per configuration, and the probability of finding a B atom at 1st, 2nd, and 3rd nearest neighbour distances from an A atom. Save the raw statistics to mc_run.log.
description: Log file containing raw MC statistics for quality assurance, not directly scored.

title: Extract monomer/dimer fractions, short-range order parameters, and output final scored JSON
action: From the MC statistics compute the ensemble-averaged monomer fraction and dimer fraction for each alloy at θ=0.15. For AuPd at θ=0.1, compute the short-range order parameter α(r) = 1 − p_AB(r)/x_B at 1st, 2nd, and 3rd nearest neighbour distances. For AuPd at θ=0.5, T=100 K, compute α at 1st nearest neighbour distance (expected to be ≈−1 reflecting c(2×2) ordering). Combine all results with the random baseline from step_01 into a single JSON file simulation_results.json containing all required fields.
description: Main scored artifact containing monomer/dimer fractions, short-range order parameters derived from Monte Carlo simulations, and the random alloy baseline.
